title: Postictal unresponsive patient at a stadium
setting: Stadium corridor. 45M collapsed after a generalized convulsive seizure which ended 2 minutes ago. Lying on his back, unresponsive but breathing normally.
verdictExplanation: Unresponsive postictal patient who is currently unable to maintain his own airway (snoring breathing and saliva in the mouth). Sick: requires immediate airway protection.

shared.danger: Hard concrete floor, spectators crowding around
shared.response: Unresponsive to voice and physical stimulus
shared.airway: Compromised by position and saliva, snoring sounds
shared.circulation: Strong pulse, skin is warm and sweaty

history.history: Crashed his bike at low speed, then suffered a 2-minute convulsive seizure which has now stopped
history.drugs: Anticonvulsant medication (forgot to take his dose today)
history.injuries: Slight bruising on his shoulder, no major visible bleeding
history.additional: Wears a medical-alert bracelet confirming epilepsy

followUp.question: What is your immediate priority management for this patient?

options.text: Place him in the recovery position immediately to clear the airway and protect from aspiration
Hold his head completely still, suspecting a spinal injury, and do not move him
Insert a finger into his mouth to clear saliva and pull his tongue forward
Attempt to wake him up by shaking him and splashing water on his face

followUp.explanation: An unresponsive patient who is breathing normally must be placed in the recovery position to keep the airway open and let saliva drain. Airway protection takes absolute precedence over potential spinal injury. Never put fingers in a patient's mouth or attempt forceful arousal.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Place in the recovery position to protect the airway. Monitor breathing continuously. Call 999 if the seizure was prolonged, recurred, or if it is his first seizure.
levelFlags.erNotes: Suspected postictal phase. Maintain airway in the recovery position. Administer high-flow oxygen due to low SpO2 (89%), check BGL, and conduct a secondary survey for injuries sustained during the fall.
